MI Faruqui with MA Wahab Mia, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party Nos. 1-3.

Gouri Rani Dutta ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Taib Ali & ors ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This Rule obtained under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.5.86 passed by Mr. TIM Nurunnabi Chowdhury, Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka rejecting the defendant- petitioner's application under Order VII rule 11(d) CPC for rejection of plaint of Title Suit No. 108 of 1986. 

 2. The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 only instituted Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 on 18.8.85 against the defendant-petitioner in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka valuing the suit as Tk. 6,000/- only praying for a declaration of 16 annas right, title, interest and possession in the suit land described in the schedule. The defendant-petitioner received notice of the suit, contested the same by filing a written statement and also contested a temporary injunction matter by filing written objection. On 27.4.86, the date fixed for hearing of injunction matter, plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application under Order XXIII rule 1(2) CPC for permission to withdraw the suit because of formal defects with liberty to sue afresh on the same cause of action. Without waiting for the disposal of the said application, the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed another suit, namely, Title Suit No. 108 of 1986 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the same cause of action against the defendant-petitioner, adding plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 as plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4 and praying for a declaratory decree decreeing title of plaintiffs in the Schedule A property which is indistinguishable from the schedule of the earlier suit. They also prayed for confirmation of possession over Schedule B property, which is a part of Schedule A property for which they wanted a declaration of title. The defendant-petitioner filed an application on 29.4.86 under Order VII rule 11(d) CPC for rejection of the plaint on the simple ground that it appears from paragraph 7 of the plaint of Title Suit No. 108 of 1986 that the plaintiffs instituted the said suit without permission to withdraw themselves from Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 with liberty to sue afresh and therefore the suit is barred under the provisions of Order XXIII rule 1(3) CPC. 

 5. Mr. Abdur Rahman, learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner, submits that except for the valuation and addition of two more plaintiffs, the subject-matter and issues in both Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 and Title Suit No. 108 of 1986 are the same. The plaintiffs have stated in paragraph 7 of the plaint of Title Suit No. 108 of 1986 that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 brought Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka for declaration of title in respect of Schedule A property, and the suit suffers from formal defects and in that view of the matter, the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 have instructed to file an application under Order XXIII rule 1(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the 6th Court of Munsif to withdraw the suit with a permission to sue afresh. 

 6. Mr. Abdur Rahman submits that the aforesaid averment brings the subsequent suit within the mischief of Order XXIII rule 1(3) which is as follows: 

 7. Mr. Abdur Rahman further submits that the application of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 for withdrawal of the suit was ultimately heard on 29.6.86. The learned Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka passed an order giving permission to the said plaintiff to withdraw the suit but no permission was given to file a fresh suit on the same cause of action. As against this order of the learned Munsif dated 29.6.86 the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed a revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division. By judgment and order dated 22.7.86 in Civil Order No. 727 of 1986, a learned single Judge of this Division summarily disposed of the application with the order that the order of withdrawal shall be deemed to be an order under Order XXIII rule (1) sub-rule (1) and that the suit was simply withdrawn. 

 8. Mr. Abdur Rahman submits that since a learned Judge of the High Court Division has ultimately refused any permission to sue afresh, the subsequent suit namely, Title Suit No. 108 of 1986, is barred under provisions of Order XXIII rule 1 (3) CPC. 

 9. Mr. M I Faruqui, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that there is absolutely no legal bar in instituting as many suits as the plaintiffs can on the same cause of action in as many different forums as he chooses. The remedy of the common defendant in the multifarious suits will be governed by section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submits that the language of section 10 is a clear enough indication that successive suits on the same cause of action in different forums is permissible in law. He submits that on the date of filing of Title Suit No.108 of 1986 on 27.4.86, the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 did not withdraw from Title Suit No. 138 of 1985. Unless and until a plaintiff withdraws from a suit, the embargo placed upon him under Order 23 rule 1 (3) CPC is not attracted. 

 10. Indeed we find that in paragraph 7 of the plaint of Title Suit No.108 of 1986 the plaintiff-opposite parties have only stated that they have applied for withdrawal of Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 with a permission to sue afresh under Order 23 rule 1 (2) CPC. They have not stated that they have already withdrawn from the said suit and there is no averment that they have withdrawn without the permission to sue afresh under Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC. It appears to us very clear that unless a suit is filed under the condition described in Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC, the bar of suit cannot be attracted. In other words, a plaintiff must be seen in the position of filing a second suit after actual withdrawal of first suit without obtaining permission to sue afresh. If he is not caught in this position then the bar of Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC is not attracted. We find considerable force in the submission of Mr. M I Faruqui that on the date that the subsequent suit was filed, the second suit was net attracted by the mischief of Order 23 rule 1 (3) CPC. 

 11. Mr. Abdur Rahman, however, submits that subsequently the plaintiff opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 withdrew the suit on 29.6.86 and up to the High Court Division they failed to obtain any permission to sue afresh. Therefore the suit that they filed on 27.4.86, namely, the instant suit, must be held to be barred under Order 23 rule 1 (3) CPC. 

 12. To this Mr. MI Faruqui submits that Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC does not bar a suit already instituted before the other suit has been abandoned or dismissed. He submits that the bar of Order 23 rule 1(3) applies only to a suit instituted after withdrawal or abandonment of previous suit. If the plaintiff opposite parties had filed Title Suit No.108 of 1986 after the learned Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka gave them a simple permission to withdraw the suit without any leave to sue afresh or after 22nd September, 1986, when the learned Judge of the High Court Division summarily disposed of their application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, then that suit would have been covered by the mischief of Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC. The instant suit having been instituted on 27.4.86, prior to the learned Munsif  permission to withdraw the suit simpliciter, the mischief of Order 23 rule 1 (3) CPC is not attracted. 

 14. It appears to us that Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC preludes the plaintiffs from instituting any fresh suit in respect of the subject matter or part of the claim of the previous suit in future, after the plaintiff withdraws from the previous suit without the permission to sue afresh. This sub-rule does not refer to a suit which has already been instituted before the plaintiff has withdrawn the previous suit. Order 23 rule 1(3) CPC is a provision barring a plaintiff from instituting further suit and its provisions cannot be given a retrospective effect when in clear terms that sub-rule speaks of a future suit. We are, therefore, in full agreement with the decision given in the Lahore case. 

 16. If it was the view of the learned Single Judge that the suit already instituted is barred under Order 23 rule 1 (3) CPC he would have accorded a permission.
